Young Iranians were waving flags from their cars, playing music loudly, and talking on the internet using the hashtag #IranTalks. They were excited because of a new nuclear agreement with the United States and other countries. This deal might end Iran's isolation and the strict economic penalties it has faced for years. Just before midnight on Thursday, Vali Asr Street, a main road in Tehran, became like a street party. Car horns were honing. Men were dancing in the traffic. Some people showed U. S. dollar bills.

According to a court document from Brooklyn, a fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, has been charged in a plot to help terrorists and for some of the men to join ISIS. The document, released on Monday, adds Kasimov to charges against three other men who were already arrested: Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. These three men are accused of providing support to a foreign terrorist organization and have pleaded not guilty. It is not known if Kasimov has been arrested.

On Saturday, North American early risers were rewarded with the third of four lunar eclipses. This one was the shortest of the series, lasting nearly five minutes. The moon entered Earth's shadow completely at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. Eastern Time). NASA says this is the shortest total lunar eclipse of the 21st century. Before, during, and after the total eclipse, the moon turned a burnt-orange color, which is why total lunar eclipses are called "blood moons."

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN) – On Tuesday, many people in Turkey were afraid and confused. "What's going on? What happened? Why can't I get into the subway?" asked an elderly woman wearing a white headscar and carrying several shopping bags. She was standing outside a blocked entrance to one of Istanbul's busiest subway stations. She was one of millions of people left confused and worried by the worst power outage in Turkey in more than ten years. Dozens of cities across Turkey lost power for several hours on Tuesday. Millions of people were affected, including passengers who were stuck on stopped trains and subways.

During this Holy Week, let us remember what the Bible says about fair and living wages. Isaiah 58.6 says that God wants us to "break the chains of injustice," "end exploitation in the workplace," "free the oppressed," and "cancel debts." The McDonald's announcement that it will raise wages for 90,000 employees is a big win for fast-food workers and for those who support them. By standing together, fast-food workers are making it less acceptable for profitable companies like McDonald's to pay such low wages that workers are stuck in poverty.

The Golden State might soon be about the color of California's lawns. Governor Jerry Brown announced on Wednesday that he is making water restrictions mandatory for residents, businesses, and farms. He ordered cities and towns in the drought-strer state to cut their water use by 25%. "We're in a new era," Brown said. "The idea of your nice little green grass getting lots of water every day, that's going to be a thing of the past." The 25% cut in usage amounts to roughly 1.5 million acre-feet of water (an acre foot of water equals about 325,000 gallons) over the next nine months, state officials said.

It is almost time for people in the UK to vote. polling stations are ready to open. This election might change how the country is governed. The campaign was very short, especially compared to the United States, where candidates spend years preparing. The result could give power to Ed Miliband’s Labour Party, taking it from David Cameron’s Conservative government. Or, leaders might struggle to make deals with smaller parties. We will know the answer when voting ends late Thursday evening.

This is the time of year when more than 2 billion Christians around the world are thinking about the death and resurrection of Jesus. This Holy Week, we are asking Christians to also think about the terrible things happening to believers today.

On Thursday, Christian college students were killed in a massacre in Kenya. Christians in other countries are also facing threats. Many Christians—and other people— are being targeted by religious extremists simply because of their faith. They are suffering crucifix, bedecapitation, stoning, forced slavery, sexual abuse, human trafficking, harassment, bombing, and being forced to leave their homes.

The Washington Post has released emails that are racist and offensive. These emails caused three employees in Ferguson, Missouri, to either quit or lose their jobs. The emails were found during a U.S. Justice Department investigation into racial bias in the city's police and courts. The messages include offensive comments about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and minorities. The Washington Post obtained the emails on Thursday through a public records request, and CNN reviewed them on Friday. The emails were between the city's top court clerk and two police officers, including Police Captain Rick Henke and a sergeant.

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia. The police found at least 55 dead dogs dumped in the bush in Queensland. According to reports, a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman from Bundaberg were charged with illegally possessing a gun. The woman, who is a licensed trainer, was also charged with getting in the way of police. The RSPCA Queensland, an animal rights group, is helping the police with the investigation.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in Wisconsin. They sold frozen pizzas, including breakfast and gluten-free options, in stores in Nichols, near Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base.

This week, their business was threatened when people confused them with Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana. That other business made national news because its owners said they would not cater a same-sex wedding. Angry people left comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza’s Facebook page and called their phone number to protest.

A complete camel skeleton, believed to have been used by Ottoman soldiers during the 17th century siege of Vienna, has been discovered under a cellar in Austria. The bones were found by archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni) while they were working at a shopping center construction site in Tulln between 2006 and 2007. Alfred Galik, an archaeozoologist, said that the partially dug-up skeleton was initially thought to be a large horse or cow. However, he noted that a quick look at the neck vertebrae, lower jaw, and hand bones immediately showed it was a camel.

Andrew Getty, the 47-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died on Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. his parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, announced the death. They asked for the media and the public to please respect the family's privacy during this difficult time. The coroner's office said the death appears to be from natural causes or an accident. Some medicine was found in Getty's home, but investigators do not know if he was taking it or what his medical history was.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 into the French Alps on March 24, which killed everyone on board. The latest report shows that he made the plane descend faster than it should have gone. This is terrifying. As the investigation continues, we will learn more about how much Lubitz hid about his mental illness, and how much help he asked for. How much did his struggle with depression affect his ability to fly? Should he have quit his job? Should his doctors have raised concerns? His case brings up important questions about people who struggle with mental illness and the shame that often comes with it.

On April 8, 2015, CNN Student News covered several stories. The show discussed a report about U.S.-Cuba relations, and then focused on California’s historic drought. They explained that the drought’s effects are increasingly likely to spread across the entire country. The program also mentioned a flu outbreak in Chicago, but clarified that it does not affect humans. Additionally, they discussed a proposed tunnel that would connect Denmark and Germany using an underwater road and rail line. Finally, the page provided a link to the transcript of today’s show and a way for viewers to request to be included in the CNN Student News Roll Call.

A man who did not want to give his name was caught because of a tattoo on his neck. The tattoo was the name "Gertrude." This was what Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said on Saturday about Kamron Taylor. Taylor is 23 years old. He was a convicted murderer who escaped from jail before being arrested overnight in Chicago. Police around Illinois had been looking for Taylor since early Wednesday. He had jumped an correctional officer at Kankakee's Jerome Combs Detention Center. Then he left with the guard's uniform and an SUV. Surveillance video was the last thing officials saw of Taylor until just before midnight Friday in Chicago. "They saw a guy that matched the description," Bukowski said.

Prince Harry, who is 30 years old and is finishing his military career, is going to Australia. He arrives on Monday for a four-week stay. The Australian military said he will work and live with soldiers in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. He has already spent time with Australian troops several times during his 10 years in the military.

The Florida Attorney General’s office announced on Thursday that two corrections officers and one former officer trainee have been charged with plotting to kill a former inmate who was about to be released from prison. These men used to work as guards in Florida prisons.

 An FBI informant met with them after going undercover to join a branch of the Ku Klux Klan called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, according to CNN affiliate WJXT. Court documents state that one of the men, Thomas Jordan Driver, told the informant that he had had a fight with the inmate and that he and another suspect, David Elliot Moran, wanted the inmate dead.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A series of intense negotiations concluded on Thursday in Lausanne. The P5+1, a group of world powers, reached a framework agreement with Iran regarding its nuclear program. It remains unclear whether this agreement will succeed. The parties have until the end of June to finalize the details and put the plan into writing. However, the talks this week were historic, especially for the otherwise frozen U.S-Iran relationship. But that's not to say they were glamorous. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

On Monday morning, an homemade bomb exploded near a United Nations vehicle in Garowe, Somalia. The blast killed six people, including four workers for UNICEF, the international children’s agency. Somalia’s President said the attack was an attack against the future of the country. The attack happened about 8 a.m. in Garowe, the capital of the Puntland region. Al-Shabaab, a terrorist group, said they were responsible for the attack. This happened after another attack on Sunday, when three African Union soldiers died in an ambush in Lower Shabelle, Somalia. The United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia reported these details.

Prince Harry of Britain arrived in Australia on Monday. He will stay there for four weeks to work with the Australian military. Before starting his work, the 30-year-old prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. There, he paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier.

A large crowd gathered outside the memorial. Some people took photos of the prince. One boy held a sign that celebrated the prince's red hair, saying, "Red Heads Rule!"

The Australian Defence Forces said last week that during his time in Australia, Harry will work and live alongside members of the Australian Army. He will spend time with several military units in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth.

Australia, a close ally of the United States, has agreed to share some intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop called the deal an "informal arrangement" focused on tracking Australians who travel to Iraq to fight for ISIS. However, one Australian lawmaker criticized the move, comparing it to "dancing with the devil." Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in twelve years over the weekend, where she met with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing agreement was announced in an interview released on Monday, which Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Tehran.

Initial tests on the flight data recorder, which is called the "black box," show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally used the controls to make the plane faster as it went down. The French air accident investigation agency, the BEA, made this announcement. The black box was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had been searching the mountainside in the French Alps for days since the crash on March 24. The BEA stated on Friday that its teams started looking into the black box's contents right after it was found.

After a 110-day chase across the ocean, the crew of a suspected poaching ship called the *Thunder* was saved by conservationists who had been following them. The story ended in the Gulf of Guinea, off the west coast of Africa. The environmental group Sea Shepherd had been tracking the *Thunder* since their ship, the *Bob Barker*, first saw it in the Southern Ocean months ago. The *Thunder* is wanted by Interpol for suspected fraud and crimes related to fishing. The chase ended when the *Bob Barker* received a distress call from the *Thunder* early Monday.

16-year-old Jason Zobott goes to Huntley High School in suburban Chicago at 7:30 a.m. every day. Most students do the same. What makes his day different is how he learns.

Huntley High has a blended learning program. This mixes online lessons with traditional classroom teaching. One third of the school’s 2,700 students are in this program. By 215, the school wants most students to join.

Zobott is a top student. He does many activities outside of school. He says the online work is easy to access. “I can learn by myself.”

Days after a terrible attack by Al-Shabaab in Garissa, Kenya, launched airstrikes against the terrorist group in Somalia. A military source told CNN that these strikes were not revenge for the massacre at Garissa University College last week, which killed nearly 150 people. The source said the attacks on Al-Shabaab bases are part of ongoing operations that began in 2011 and are not a response to the Garissa attack. The source spoke on Monday. It is common for Kenyan military sources to remain anonymous when speaking to the media.

Pope Francis gave a traditional speech after Easter Mass. He reminded the world that the Vatican is its own country, and he spoke about his role as a moral leader. The Pope expressed sadness about the suffering of people in current conflicts. He called for an end to violence everywhere. He specifically asked for the fighting to stop in Iraq and Syria and for humanitarian aid to reach those who need it. He said, "May the international community not stand by before the immense humanitarian tragedy unfolding in these countries and the drama of the numerous refugees." These words were part of his "urbi et orbi" address, which is Latin for "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

On Wednesday afternoon, Duke University students and teachers marched together, chanting, “We are not afraid. We stand together.” This happened after a rope noose was found hanging from a tree on campus. Duke officials asked anyone who knows about the noose to call campus police. The noose was discovered near a student center at 2 a.m. Photos of the noose were shared on social media, and caused anger and upset among the community. Dozens of people gathered on the steps of Duke Chapel, which is close to where the noose was found. At a meeting there, people said, “You came here because you want to say with me, ‘This is not the Duke we will accept. This is not the Duke we want. This is not the Duke we are here to

Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, a 29 U.S. citizen who has been accused of having connections with al Qaeda, appeared in court on Thursday. He did not enter a plea to the charges against him. He is accused of conspiring to provide material support to terrorists. Al Farekh was deported from Pakistan to the United States. He is accused of plotting to fight against American forces abroad, according to a complaint unsealed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn. "This is news for celebration," said CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd.

The Saudi state news agency reported that a Saudi border guard was killed in a gunfight with militants in Yemen this week. This is the first known military death from Saudi Arabia’s side since it started bombing rebels in Yemen. The fight happened on Wednesday night in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. The news agency said that militants in a mountainous area of Yemen shot at Saudi border soldiers, and the soldiers shot back. The guard, named Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki, was killed. and 10 other people were hurt, but their injuries are not life-threatening.

I felt nervous about going to the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. Because I is the only Gulf national on the CNN team, people expect me to know about camel racing, which is an old tradition in the area. Even though I tried to wear a kandora, which is traditional clothing in the UAE, I still feel like an outsider because my modern way of life is different from this world. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis, which is a meeting room. The camel owners were gathering there. The large room looked like a fancy theater. The owners sat on the floor eating a'aish, a traditional Arabic dish made of fish and rice, which was placed in front of them. The conversation was loud and exciting.

Havana, Cuba (CNN) – Charlie Hill sits in a dark bar on a bright sunny day in Havana. "Hey man," he says, his voice rough from smoking, and he nods as if he knows you’ve been looking for him. But many people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time. For 43 years, Cuba has protected Hill from facing charges for killing a New Mexico police officer and hijating an airplane to Havana. Hill, now 65, decided to give CNN an interview after we spent two years trying to reach him. He wants to talk about how he is now considering leaving his safe place and returning to the United States for the first time.

Misao Okawa, who was recognized by Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, died at the age of 117. She passed on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan. Tadahi Uchimura, a local official, told CNN about her death. Okawa leaves behind three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren.

 Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family owned a kimono shop in Osaka. Satoshi Yoshioka, who works at the nursing home where Okawa has lived since 1997, told CNN. "She was a kind person and loved to eat a lot. Her favorite foods were sushi and udon noodles," Yoshioka said. "She ate a lot of cake for her birthday

Documents obtained by CNN show that the Missouri National Guard, as they were preparing to deploy to Ferguson, Missouri, last year, used highly militarized language to describe protesters, calling them "enemy forces" and "adversaries." The guard was sent to Ferguson to support law enforcement officers, who many community leaders and civil rights activists accused of using excessive force and inflaming an already tense situation in protests that flared sporically from August through the end of the year.

On Tuesday, gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. This attack was two parts: a car bomb and a shooting. At least 12 people died and 16 others were hurt.

 The Islamic militant group Al-Shabaab said they were responsible for the attack. A spokesman for the group, Abu Musab, made the claim.

 The attack started when two suicide bombers blew up their car at the entrance of the two-story building. The building houses the Ministry of Education, Culture, and Higher Education. A spokesman for the Somali National Security Ministry, Mohamed Yusuf, said this. Then, five gunmen went into the building and shot people inside.

Gregory Margolin, now 87, fought in World War II as a 16-year-old Jewish soldier in the Soviet Red Army. While he was fighting the Nazis, his family fled. Margolin says he did not reveal that he was Jewish, but it did not matter because people were being killed all around him. This year, in Ukraine, he found himself again surrounded by war. Margolin was a sniper who rose to be a commander in the army. His old uniform is still adorned with medals from his time in the military. His granddaughter Liora still marvels at his stories from the war. She is amazed that he managed to survive.

365 days have gone by since more than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls were taken from their school in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria. They are still missing. The Nigerian government and the world have not done enough to help them. This is shameful. It is shameful that criminals can hurt young girls without being punished. It is also shameful that people quickly forget about these terrible events.

Norway is becoming the first country in the world to stop using FM radio. In two years, the country will completely switch to digital radio. This change is happening because digital radio is replacing FM, just as video replaced radio in the past.

Norwegian listeners will not lose access to radio; they will simply need to use digital technology to listen. The government says that many of the 5 million people in Norway have already made this switch. While there are only five stations available on FM, there are four times as many stations on the Digital Audio Broadcasting network. According to Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey, half of the country now listens to radio digitally.

Everyone is excited about a good comeback story, especially when it involves a dinosaur. A new study suggests that the Brontosaurus should have its own name. For over a hundred years, its name was removed from science books.

The Brontosaurus was first named by O.C Marsh in 1879. He named it after receiving 55 crates of bones found at Como Bluff in Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. The Brontosaurus was similar to the Apatosaurus, which was discovered a few years earlier, but it was not quite as large. Marsh called it "Brontosaurus," which means "thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda has offered a reward of 2 kilograms of gold (about $774,000) for the death or capture of two prominent Shia Muslim leaders in Yemen. The group, known as Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), made the offer in an online news release and wanted poster. The targets are Houthi leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. AQAP called them the "two heads of evil." AQAP is one of several groups fighting to control Yemen.

Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old postal worker from Florida, wrote about his plans and reasons for flying a gyrocopter onto the Capitol lawn on Wednesday on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. He said his goal was to expose corruption in Washington, D.C., and to offer solutions to the problem of corruption. He wrote in an online post titled "Your Pilot" that his flight was not a secret. He said he sent an email to info@barackobama.com before taking off. The email was meant to convince the people in charge of the Capitol that he was not a threat and that shooting him down would be more trouble than letting him deliver his letters to Congress.

The problems for Rio de Janeiro before the 2016 Olympics continue. many dead fish found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. The city’s legislative assembly started an investigation on Monday to find out why the fish died. They will look into what happened in the lagoon and other lakes and bays in the state where this has happened. The investigation will work with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Environment Secret.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But he is just now getting used to the normal world. Small things like using a fork, going out at night, and going to bed without someone checking on him are all new to him. This is because he spent nearly 30 years on death row in Alabama. Until last week, when his murder convictions were canceled, and Hinton walked out of a county jail in Birmingham. "I have to pinch myself to tell myself that I'm free," he told CNN's Brooke Baldwin on Friday. "It's going to take a little time, but I'll get used to it." Hinton had to get used to much worse. For 30 years, he spent most of his time locked in a 5-by-7

After the UK election debate, opinion polls showed that there was no clear winner. The seven party leaders were: David Cameron (Conservatives), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage (UK Independence Party), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (Scottish National Party), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru, the Welsh Nationalists). Comres, which made the debate for ITV, showed that Cameron, Miliband, and Farage tied for first place with 21% and Sturgeon was close behind with 20%. ICM, for The Guardian, showed that Miliband was 25, Cameron was 24, Farage was 19, and Sturgeon was 17.

Facebook might soon need to add a new relationship status option: "Just got served divorce papers." because a New York judge ruled that using social media to serve divorce papers is legal. A woman from Brooklyn, Ellanora Arthur Baidoo, used Facebook to serve her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku, with a summons for divorce. Baidoo has been trying to get a divorce for several years, according her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell. They could not find Blood-Dzraku to give him the papers in person. Court documents say Baidoo has been able to call her husband, and he has told her that he does not have a fixed address or a job.

It sounds like a scene from a science fiction movie. A person gets a terrible accident, and they are in the hospital, brain dead, and on life support. The doctors ask the family to donate organs. Instead of saving eight lives, the family is asked to give the whole body to save just one person. Maybe a person who can’t move their body but has a strong mind. Dr. Sergio Canavero, an Italian doctor, says we are close to making this happen. HEAVEN is a project name for putting a head on a new body. HEAVEN stands for head anastomation venture. anastomation means joining two parts together in surgery.

Anthony Stokes’s story was expected to be a happy one, but it ended in tragedy on Tuesday, according to police. The teenager, who had received a heart transplant, was involved in a series of crimes. He stole a car, broke into a house, and shot at an elderly woman. He then led police on a high-speed chase before crashing his car into a pole and dying.

 In 2323, Stokes’s family told reporters that an Atlanta hospital had refused to give him a new heart. The hospital said in a letter that Stokes had a history of not following medical instructions. At that time, Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family.

It was before sunrise at Garissa University College in Kenya. Most students were still asleep in their beds. A few had already up for early morning Christian prayers. Then the attack began.

 Around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday (10:30 p.m. ET Wednesday), there was an explosion and gunshots at the front gate of the school. The attackers continued shooting as they walked through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians had gathered and took people hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray, 25, was buried at New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang as a large crowd gathered to remember him. Gray died in police custody 15 days after his arrest on a weapons charge. He suffered a serious spinal injury, which caused widespread anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray’s death is the most recent in a series of high-profile deaths of African-Americans involving law enforcement. People have demanded answers about what happened to Gray. His funeral was attended by civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody.

I have worked as a chef since I was 14, but I started fighting for food policy changes much later. In 2007, a young girl my wife was mentoring was found looking through trash for food. This inspired me to start Food Policy Action and get involved in politics. I now work on many food issues, including hunger and factory farms. I haven’t worked alone on this. One big reason for change was "The Meatrix," a 2003 cartoon that made fun of the movie "The Matrix." It was made by the GRACE Communications Foundation. It showed the health and environmental dangers of factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor, so he has seen many patients die in hospitals. They were often on strong pain medication and very worried. he has also watched people suffer for weeks or months while their families stood by, unable to help. Now, this topic is personal for him. In 213, he was diagnosed with a rare, advanced cancer. Surgees removed parts of his pancreas and liver, along with his entire sple and gallbl. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48, knows the cancer is likely to come back.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against Houthi rebels and supporters of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh in Aden. The special forces were on the ground in non-combat roles, " coordinating and guiding" the battle against Houthi forces. They also helped parachute in weapons and communications equipment. Houthi rebels, meanwhile, withdrew from the presidential palace and other key parts of the southern port city of Aden following heavy Saudi airstrikes, according to the source. The withdrawal signaled a reversal from rebel gains the previous day, when Houthi forces seized the presidential palace.

A woman from Detroit, Mitchelle Angela Blair, was charged in court this week with murder and torture. This happened last month when police found the bodies of two of her children inside a freezer.

Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy says Blair killed her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

 Detroit Police Chief James Craig said that on March 24, a court worker who was there to evate the family found the bodies wrapped in plastic inside the freezer.

 The medical examiner for Wayne County has said that Stoni died from multiple blunt trauma injuries and Stephen from multiple blunt trauma and thermal injuries.

Wladimir Klitschko, the current world heavyweight boxing champion, has a big title fight coming up. However, he is mostly thinking about the ongoing struggle for democracy in his home country, Ukraine. Klitschko spoke to CNN from his training base in Miami, before his match with American challenger Bryant Jennings on April 25 in New York. He said that the crisis in his homeland has left him shocked and upset. "My country is unfortunately suffering in the war with Russia -- not that Ukraine tried to give any aggression to any other nation, in this particular case Russia, unfortunately it's the other way around," Klitschko told CNN.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" this weekend, making a small reference to his famous roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman." This was his third time hosting the show. He joked in his opening speech that a lot has changed since he first hosted in 1822. He said, "I have a 31-year-old son. I also have a 28-year-old girlfriend."

Some fans were disappointed because they wanted to see him act out his famous characters. SNL cast members Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan sang a song asking him to play Batman and Beetlejuice with them. He only responded with a few short jokes.

About a month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois court. On Wednesday morning, he was in an Illinois jail. He hid outside his cell, waiting to attack. He beat up a guard who was checking the cells, put on the guard’s uniform, and took his keys. Then he walked out of the jail and got into the guard’s brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old, who was supposed to be sentenced in May, is now missing. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m. in some time zones).

A New York City detective has been suspended because he is accused of stealing $300 during a raid on illegal cigarettes. Police spokesman Stephen Davis made the announcement. Surveillance video from News 12 Brooklyn shows Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn last Friday. The detectives had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store’s manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed that money was missing from a box. He thought one of his employees had taken it. When he checked the security cameras, he was shocked by what he saw, he told News 12 Brooklyn.

The Hatton Garden burglary, which will likely be remembered as a major crime, was a terrible experience for safe deposit box owners and a exciting scene for movie directors. Thies used heavy cutting tools and climbing gear to break into the vault of a well-known, 60-year-old safe deposit company in central London over the holiday weekend. They may have had up to four days to search through many safe deposit boxes. They reportedly stole hundreds of thousands of pounds worth of jewelry and cash. One former police official guessed the total value could be as high as 200 million pounds, or $300 million.

On April 27, South Africa marks the anniversary of the first elections after apartheid in 1994. This year, we are facing another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. People are expressing their anger on social media using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica, showing that we need to stand together against this violence. These repeated attacks on migrants and their homes suggest that South Africa’s dream of unity is failing. That dream was about a country where people of all races and backgrounds live with dignity.

In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, said he was “drinking poison” when he accepted a ceasefire to end the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had helped define Khomeini’s regime, the Islamic Republic, which he had founded a year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini galvanized the nation, both his supporters and growing opponents, to fight against the enemy. He dragged out the war for eight years, despite Saddam’s willingness to accept a ceasefire, and thus stabilized the foundations of the Islamic Republic. By the time he ended the war, the economy was in shambles, and there was no sign of his die-hard volunteers.

The idea of sustainable development is that unchecked capitalism is too powerful for its own good. The global economy is growing very fast, doubling in size every generation. But this growth is happening on a finite Earth, where the population increases by a billion people every 15 years. This rapid growth is damaging the natural resources and social systems that make life good and decent. Sustainable development offers a way out of this crisis. The truth is that unchecked capitalism is driven by greed.

The United States has many benefits from being a space-faring nation. U.S. access to space has provided incredible benefit to U.S. national security, defense and the economic well-being of the nation. And in order to effectively confront current and future conflicts, combat terrorism and counter the proliferating threats worldwide, our military depends on space-based capabilities, including intelligence, GPS, and communications satellites. Unfortunately, as global threats increase and the need for assured space access accelerates, the U.S. is faced with a troubling reality -- we are far too reliant on Russian technology to meet our national security obligations.

On the day before the one-year anniversary of the kidnapping of nearly 300 schoolgirls in Nigeria by Boko Haram, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to them. The 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner said that she was also a target of militants who wanted to stop girls from going to school. She survived an attack by the Taliban in Pakistan because she wrote about the importance of staying in school. In her letter, she asked the Nigerian government and the world to do more to rescue the girls. Nigeria recently held an election.

On Tuesday evening, South African soldiers were sent in to help the government stop deadly attacks against immigrants. Their first mission was in Jeppestown, a neighborhood in Johannesburg where the violence started on Friday. While the soldiers guarded the area, police raided a hostel there. Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula announced that some soldiers would be sent to places where police are stretched too thin and trying to stop the deadly attacks against immigrants. "This intervention is not an indictment on the police. ..."

According to Iranian state media, eight Iranian border guards died in fighting with militants near the Pakistan border. Iranian forces killed three of the militants in the town of Negur on Monday. IRNA, the state news agency, reported this, citing Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province. Mirshekari said the militants crossed into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistan to help catch the attackers who survived the fighting.

Providenciales, in the Turks and Caicos, has been named the number one island in the world by TripAdvisor. It was last year's second choice. It now beats Ambergris Caye, which was previously number one. Ambergris Caye had been the top island for two years, but it has now fallen out of the top ten. A TripAdvisor spokesperson, Julie Cassetina, said it is hard to say why it disappeared, because the winners change each year based on traveler feedback.

The "Star Wars" story continues to grow. at a fan event in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, the plot for the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" was made public. Director Gareth Edwards showed an early preview of the film and shared details about the story. Disney calls this type of movie an "anthfilm" instead of "spinoff." Felicity Jones stars in the movie. The story happens after "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and before "Episode IV: A New Hope" (which is the first "Star Wars" movie from 1777). A group of rebels goes on a secret mission to steal plans for the Death Star. Jones plays a rebel soldier.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) There is a Persian saying: "A good year is determined by its spring." For many Iranians, the historic decision by Tehran and six world powers—the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, and and China—to continue nuclear talks under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" is a sign that this year's Norouz, the Persian New Year that started on March 21, will be a superb one indeed. Although edged hardliners may now try to play games and complain the preliminary agreement is not what they had hoped, for many people it shows excellent progress and that's what they want.

On Wednesday night, one person died and another was hurt in a suspected terrorist attack near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. The police say a 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove his car into two people who were waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill area. The driver has been arrested and is being questioned by the General Security Services. Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died in the hospital. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition.

The art collection of the late actress Lauren Bacall has been put for sale. The collection, which includes works by some of the greatest 20th-century artists, was auction in New York on March 31. It had previously been shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles. Bacall, who died in August 214 at age 89, became famous in 114 with her first film, "To Have and Have Not." That same year, she met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the 2015 Golden Globes, George Clooney paid tribute to the silver screen queen in his award-winning speech.

People in Kiev, Ukraine, are worried about who might killing people who were close to Ukraine’s former President, Viktor Yanukovych. This fear has been around for a while, but it became a big concern this week after two famous people were shot and killed in Kiev. One was a former politician who worked with Yanukovych, and the other was a journalist who supported Russia. Oleg Kalashnikov, the former politician, was shot and died shortly after 7 p.m. on Wednesday when he arrived at his apartment building.

Chile will soon recognize same-sex civil unions. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday. Chile is now one of several South American countries that allows these unions. Bachelet said this is an important step toward treating gay and heterosexual couples equally. The law will start in six months. It gives legal recognition to cohab relationships between two people of the same sex, or between a man and a woman. The government says about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

When you fly to Florida, look out the window. If you are visiting Disney World or going to Miami, sit by the window and look at the land below. The Everglades show how mistakes can cost a lot of money to fix. When you fly into Miami or Orlando, the area looks like a messy swamp full of dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. One researcher once caught 365,000 bugs in just one trap in one night.

In early April, ISIS militants took over the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. They came in large numbers, wearing masks, and quickly control the area. The camp had already been under attack by Syrian forces for more than two years, and the residents were already suffering. Now, they faced a new and even more frightening reality: ISIS had defeated other armed groups in the area and taken control. One resident, who asked not to be named, told CNN that ISIS fighters killed people in the streets. He said they caught three people and killed them in front of others. ISIS now controls almost all of the camp.

According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors have found their "Great Firewall" isn't enough anymore. They have developed a new cyber weapon called the "Great Cannon." This tool attacks servers located outside of China, including those in the United States. It operates openly. The study's authors believe that this visible attack on other countries' servers will likely anger the international community, and they suggest that Beijing may have expected this to happen.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any evidence of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz committed the act. However, a spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday that Lubitz had suicidal tendencies before he started his career as a pilot.

 Investigators have not found any writings or conversations where Lubitz explained his reasons or admitted to any plans, according to prosecutor’s spokesman Christoph Kumpa. Medical records show that Lubitz was suicidal at one point and received psychotherapy. This happened before he ever got his pilot’s license, Kumpa said.

On Sunday, the leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels said his group would not surrender. Abdul-Malik al-Houthi told people on television that his fighters will not leave the main cities or government buildings. He said that anyone who thinks they will give up is dreaming.

 This statement came after more than three weeks of airstrikes by a Saudi-led coalition. A top Saudi military official said these attacks have significantly weakened the Houthi group. The Houthsi group, who are Shiite Muslims, took over the capital city of Sanaa in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a large truck bomb into the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people, including men, women, and children, and and hurt hundreds more. It is the worst act of homegrown terrorism in United States history. The news about the bombing was everywhere, with stories talking about how it hit the middle of the country and how America felt like it had lost its innocence. The bombing really shocked the country. People were not just surprised by how many people died, but also by the fact that an American citizen had attacked the government with such deadly force, something that had never been seen before.

 A year ago, Boko Haram militants kidnapped more than 200 Nigerian girls from their school. People all around the world wanted them back safely, so they joined a social media campaign. Charles Alasholuyi was one of them. Celebrities and world leaders also spoke out in anger using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. It was one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 2021, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, the missing girls were still not found. The campaign’s attention faded.

Barney Frank, a retired U.S. Congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He told the full audience about his 45 years in public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while holding office. He also criticized politicians who hide their support for LGBT rights while voting against them. When an audience member asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he did not know about it. He told the young man not to worry about "crazy people."

Al-Shabaab militants attacked Garissa University College in Kenya on Thursday morning. during morning prayers. The attackers shot people randomly and took hostages. nearly 150 people were killed, including students, and dozens more were injured. Security forces eventually killed the attackers. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said that Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. This attack happened only a few months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been responsible for many attacks in the area. They have also recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa has removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonial leader. This happens after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town started a campaign on social media last month. They used the hashtag #RhodesMustFall to demand the statue be taken down. They said Rhodes’ history is connected to racism. The campaign was successful, and the hashtag is now #RhodesHasFallen. The university announced on Wednesday that a heritage authority gave permission to remove the statue from the campus. The university said the statue is being moved to keep it safe while they decide what to do with it in the future.

Syria is becoming a terrible place, and the situation is getting worse. According to an opposition group, the number of people killed has doubled in just one year. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported on Thursday that 310,00 people have died since the civil war began. A year before that, the number was 162,402. The year before that, the United Nations said 70,000 people had died. The UN says that more than half of Syrians are so poor that they desperately need help to survive. Food rations are being cut because there are not enough donations.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly, looking almost shy. But prosecutors say she was not afraid to fight a rival. A criminal complaint says she threatened a woman in a phone call this summer. She told the woman, "Leave my man alone" and "Stop looking for him." She also said, "I know people that can put a bomb where you live." Because of who she is, prosecutors did not think it was a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment. She denies the charges. Last December, when she left court, she and her lawyer would not talk about the case. Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

A police officer in Gaza told CNN that police took a door with a drawing by British artist Banksy on Thursday. This happened after a disagreement about the sale. The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, went to a court in Gaza. He said he did not know the door was valuable when he sold it for only $175. The police in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, will keep the iron door. They will return it after a court hearing, which has not been scheduled yet. Darduna said that when his home in Gaza was destroyed in last summer’s war, he felt he had lost everything. except a doorway and a door.

The Saudi-led coalition’s attacks on Houthi rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. The coalition is gaining control, while many locals are fleeing the violence and the number of deaths is rising, including dozens of civilians.

 Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition has destroyed the Houthi air defense systems and the air defenses of supporters of Yemen’s former President, Ali Abdullah Saleh. A Saudi source said that all but a small number of air bases and runways are now unusable. The source also said that Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all Yemeni ports. allowing only closely monitored non-military medical supplies to pass through the blockade.

Guus Hiddink, the manager of the Netherlands team, strongly criticized his own fans for booing Andres Iniesta during the Netherlands' 2-0 win against Spain on Tuesday. He called the fans a "disgrace."

Iniesta, who started on the bench, came into the game in the 76th minute. The home fans cheered and booed him.

Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored goals in the first half, giving the Netherlands a good win. However, Hiddink was unhappy about how Iniesta was treated.

On May 21, Scotland will learn if its Euro 2016 match against Georgia in September will be played without any fans in the stadium. UEFA has started disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation (GFF) because fans entered the field twice during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi. UEFA also plans to investigate other charges, including claims that home fans set off fireworks. and several safety violations, such as blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff not doing body searches at the Boris Paichadze Stadium. A fan ran onto the field during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

On Wednesday, football agents were waiting to hear about new rules. starting April 1, the rules for becoming a football agent will change. Anyone can become an agent if they pay £550 for the first year. After that, the Football Association (FA) will charge £250 each year to renew the license. This does not apply to agents who already have a license. The FA plans to put a link on their website for agents to sign up, but by 1pm the link was not yet available. Mel Stein believes the new rules will cause chaos. These new guidelines come after FIFA stopped controlling how agents are regulated.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not received his salary for three months. Since joining the club in January on an 18-month contract, he has not been paid. He has had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Despite these money problems, Uvarenko likes the fans. He says they are unique and give passionate support. He told local media on Wednesday that the lack of money is his biggest problem at CSKA.

A driver punched a father who was taking his child to school, then broke his car with a hockey stick. This happened in front of young children because he was having a 'bad day' and saw red, a court has heard. Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This sad result reminds people of Spain’s terrible performance at the 2014 World Cup. Gerard Pique says that coach Vicente del Bosque should not be too worried about losing three friend games in a row.

Holland won 5-1 against Spain in the group stage of the World Cup in Brazil last year. that game ended Spain’s six-year rule as the best team in the world. Holland scored two goals early in the game at the Amsterdam Arena. They kept Spain from scoring in the second half, even though Spain tried hard, and won 2-0.

Police say a New York City mother, Ulrike Berger, 44, has taken her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, to Germany during a custody dispute. A court order forb Berger from leaving the United States with the child. On March 22, one day after Kaia was dropped off for a weekend visit, the two are believed to have boarded a flight to Europe. Police are searching for Berger and Kaia. They believe the pair flew from New York to Germany on March 22, breaking the custody court order. Police say the last time they saw the two was at Berger’s home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10 a.m. on March 21, when Kaia’s father dropped her off.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast of Britain. The flames and thick smoke filled the sky. The fire destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches. This happened after several days of storms that knocked down trees and closed roads. The 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside and water ran off the slope. Fire investigators said the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas of heheland were destroyed: one was half a hectare, another was one hectare, and the largest was 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services in Britain received 600 calls per hour during New Year’s Eve 2012 celebrations. Paramedics were overwhelmed. In Cambridge, the Terrial Army set up a field hospital to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said they handled over 600 calls per hour at the peak, which is more than three times the usual number. In Manchester, a man collapsed on the sidewalk next to an ambulance while two people walked by eating late-night food. In another Manchester scene, a man stood slumped in a doorway while two women walked by celebrating New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says that his strong mind helped him get over being dropped from the team last December. Manager Brendan Rodgers stopped playing Mignolet in December because he was not playing well. Mignolet came back quickly when another player, Brad Jones hurt his thigh. The 27-year-old Belgian player said he tried to stay positive even though he was upset about being removed from the team. Mignolet told FourFourTwo magazine, "I stayed positive."

On Tuesday, large hailstones, as big as plums, fell in the Southern United States. people outside to record the unusual weather. Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed ice balls hitting his backyard and splashing into his swimming pool. The video shows the hailstones falling quickly and breaking when they hit the ground. It was about 80 degrees outside, but the hard ice took a long time to melt. In just a few seconds, the patio was covered in white ice.

The crew of a replica pirate ship, the Liana's Ransom, was forced to leave their vessel after it lost power in rough seas off the coast of Maine.

The Coast Guard rescued nine crew members using lifeboats on Tuesday.

The Canadian charter ship was left drifting 30 miles east of Portland, according to Coast Guard officials.

The tall ship reported engine problems around 12:35 a.m. on Monday. The crew also said that the sails had become wrapped around the mast.

Amazing photos show blue glowing algae along Australia's east coast. The pictures were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales. The bright neon light lit up one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson called the sight a "beautiful supernatural scene" caused by millions of tiny floating plants (plankton) giving off light. A similar event happened at Sydney's Manly Beach in August 214. An ocean expert told Daily Mail Australia that people should not worry about the algae.

17 Rahul Kumar, a drunk teenager, was rescued by security guards after he jumped into a lion enclosure at a zoo in western India. The incident happened at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad. Kumar climbed over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting that he would "kill them." He later explained that he was drunk and thought he had a "good chance" against the animals. While sitting near the enclosure, he suddenly ran toward the lions, shouting, "Today I kill a lion!" and surprised the zoo security staff.

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, China, survived after falling from a fifth-story window onto a car. The incident happened last Saturday. his father believes the boy fell while sleepwalking. A hotel receptionist across the street heard a loud bang around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Drew Miller, a player for the Detroit Red Wings, said he is excited to play again. He got a cut on his face just one day ago. The cut could have made him blind. Miller said he feels lucky that the hockey stick did not hit his eye. He spoke at practice on Wednesday. He wore a full face mask. His face had a bad wound. It needed 50 or 60 stitches to close. The stitches went through several layers of skin. The Detroit Free Press reported this. Miller has a scar near his eye. He did not lose his eyesight. Another player cut his face.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends next year, even though Atletico Madrid might try to bring him back this summer. He joined Chelsea from Atletico last July on a three-year deal, but he has had a hard time becoming the team’s regular left defender. Atletico might use this to get a better deal if they sign him again, but Luis says he is happy at Chelsea and wants to stay there.

22-year-old Charlie Sumner, a fan of Reading Football Club, is facing a three-year ban from football. He was topless and doing somersaults on the field during his first game at the Madejski Stadium. Sumner ran onto the pitch during the FA Cup quarter-final replay match between Reading and Bradford City last month. Reading won 3-0. Sumner was on the field when his team was leading 3-0. He performed four front flips and landed on his back. Stewards then tackled him. Sumner said going to his first game was a "brilliant experience." Now he faces a possible three-year ban for his stunt.

A video shows a van carrying about six men on its roof swerving and then tipping over. The accident happened on a road near Salé, Morocco. The van was likely carrying football fans. A car following the van recorded the scary footage. The video shows the van moving side to side on a busy road before it falls onto its side.

England’s Under-17 soccer team plays in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships. The tournament is in Bulgaria in May. They are playing against the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy.

 England is the current champion. They won last year’s final in Malta by beating Holland on penalties. To move on to the quarter-finals, England must beat Holland again. This year’s tournament has 16 teams, up from eight last year.

 Danny Collinge scored England’s first goal against Norway during the qualifying matches.

An elephant was relaxing by a small pool in South Africa’s Kruger National Park with its family. A male buffalo came too close, which made the elephant angry. The elephant tried to spray water from its trunk at the buffalo to make it leave, but it missed. The baby elephant stayed close to its parent for protection while the buffalo drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub owner, won an eight-year legal battle to overturn his conviction for showing foreign TV channels that broadcast Premier League soccer games. Thorpe, 55, was convicted in November 206 at the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon, for showing a Premier League game without a license from the official broadcasters. He says the long fight cost him dearly, including the loss of his pub.

The Irish Football Association (IFA) is worried about structural damage at Windsor Park, their stadium in Belfast. They hope that the problem does not prevent them from hosting a very important Euro 2016 soccer match against Romania in June. The IFA found cracks in the West Stand on Tuesday morning. They closed off that area while engineers checked the damage. A spokesman for the IFA said they learned about the damage that happened overnight on Monday night.

Sumner went onto the pitch at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup quarter-final replay against Bradford City last month. Reading was winning 3-0 at the time. Sumner did four front flips, landing on his back each time, before being tackled by security guards.

A BMW driver was arrested today after a student was hit and killed while walking to the library. The driver had five children in the car. Hina Shamim, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London last night. She was only weeks away from her 22th birthday. Friends left flowers at the scene today. They said Miss Shamim, who was from Peterborough and went by the nickname Hyena, was very much loved and a very nice and charming girl. Hina Shamim was killed when she was hit while walking a short distance from her home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested because a video of them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston was posted online. The video was recorded on Tuesday. The mother, who has not been named, was reportedly angry because the student had allegedly been bullying her daughter. The Channel 2 news reported this. In the video, the mother is wearing a black top and is on the right, while the victim is in the center wearing white.

Stoke City’s chief executive, Tony Scholes, hopes they can keep Asmir Begovic, the team’s goalkeeper. Begovic is in the final year of his contract. The player from Bosnia has been linked with other clubs while playing at the Britannia Stadium. Although his contract has just over 12 months left, Scholes believes they can match the 27-year-old’s ambitions. “Clearly Asmir is a terrific goalkeeper and we are very keen to keep him at the club,” he told The Sentinel. “I think when you’ve got extremely good players it is only natural that there will be speculation about their future.”

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was fired by his boss for reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver turning the pages of the newspaper while the bus was moving and stopped at a traffic light. The passenger sent the video and a complaint to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines. The company’s boss, Andrew Ritchie, called the driver a “complete idiot” and said he was embarrassed by what the driver did.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says defender Winston Reid will play on Saturday against Leicester City, because they are the last team in the league. Reid has been injured since March 4, when West Ham lost 1-0 to Chelsea. He hurt his hamstring. But during the break for international games, he came back to full practice.

Enner Valencia will not play. He missed the last two games, against Arsenal and Sunderland. He hurt his toe in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is not ready to play yet.

Five days before his wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a terrible car crash on a highway in Georgia. Brittany died, and John was badly hurt. Doctors said John might spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and use a wheelchair. The 25-year-old, who was an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College, had a very difficult future ahead of him. But against the odds, John got better. On March 24, he helped his team win a championship title.

Lucas, playing on the left, was seen with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard at the All-Star charity game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a midfielder for Liverpool, wants to get back to his best form after recovering from an injury. This is the best form he has had in two years.

The Brazilian player started 16 of 19 games from late November. During this time, the team’s results got much better. However, he hurt his groin in February during the match against Everton (the Merseyside derby) and missed 10 games because of it.
